subject: Cognitive Science
title: Constraints Boost Creativity
description: A quick, practical guide to Constraints Boost Creativity.

hook.text: Dr. Seuss wrote Green Eggs and Ham using only 50 words. The constraint forced extreme creativity.

buildup.text: Counterintuitively, fewer resources and tighter rules often produce more creative outcomes.

discovery.text: Constraints reduce the search space—limiting options forces the brain to explore novel combinations.

twist.text: Total freedom is paralyzing. "Write anything" produces less than "write a six-word memoir."

climax.text: Twitter's character limit, haiku's syllable rules, and sonnet structure all prove that limits unlock invention.

punchline.text: Limits don't kill creativity. They spark it.

quiz.question: Why do constraints boost creativity?
options: They force the brain to explore novel combinations
